title: Runway Accelerator KPI Calendar & Contingency Playbook
content:
Purpose:
A compact, operational KPI calendar and contingency playbook intended to guide the cross-functional launch for the Runway Accelerator initiative (beta -> GA). This is a living sheet used during the 8-week ramp: owners update metrics daily during high-risk phases and weekly otherwise.

Primary goals:
- Keep request latency (p95) within target while scaling throughput 4x during pilot.
- Hold per-token cost delta to < 15% vs baseline through batching + quantization.
- No customer-facing SLA breach during staged traffic increase.

Snapshot KPIs (baseline vs target):
- Avg latency (p95) baseline: 220ms -> target: <= 140ms
- Error rate (5xx) baseline: 0.6% -> target: <= 0.2%
- Cost per 1k tokens baseline: $2.80 -> target: <= $3.20 (temporary bump OK if latency improves)
- Embedding throughput (req/min) baseline: 1,200 -> ramp target: 5,000
- Cache hit ratio baseline: 6% -> target: 28% (prefix caching tuned)

Traffic mix and threshold calendar (simplified):
- Week 0 (canary, 0.5% traffic): observe p95, 5xx, and kv-cache hit. Trigger -> expand if stable 48h.
- Week 1-2 (beta, 1-5%): validate autoscaling, canary rollback policy in place. Trigger to pause if 5xx > 0.5% for 30m or p95 > 300ms for 15m.
- Week 3-4 (staged ramp, 5-25%): enable dedicated GPU pool burst; monitor token cost horizon. Trigger to scale down model size or enable quantized variant if cost delta > 20% sustained 24h.
- Week 5-8 (broad rollout, 25-100%): final rollback gates; run chaos drills for region failover.

Capacity commitments (owner-run):
- Dedicated GPU pool: reserve 12 A100-equivalent slots (initial), escalate to 24 on Week 3 if throughput trend > 70% capacity. Owner: Marco Alvarez.
- Hosted burst quota: request uplift from infra market by Day -7. Owner: Liam O'Neill.
- Observability retention: extended traces for canary cohort (14d). Owner: Sana Patel.

Runbook: triggers -> immediate actions (short):
- Trigger A: p95 > 300ms for 10m
  - Action 1: Switch traffic to lower-context variant (model-v1-lite) -> 5m (owner: Marco)
  - Action 2: Increase batch window by 20ms for background traffic -> 2m (owner: Marco)
- Trigger B: 5xx > 0.5% sustained 30m
  - Action 1: Rollback to previous stable model version (pin by tag) -> 10m (owner: Zoe)
  - Action 2: Open incident channel, escalate to SRE mobile on-call -> immediate (owner: SRE lead)
assumptions:
- Baseline numbers reflect last-stable GA traffic (Nov 2024).
- Model variants are performance-tested in staging; quantized variants may show slight quality regressions that are acceptable for non-critical paths.
- Cost targets allow temporary 10-20% overshoot during staged ramp to avoid latency spikes.
quick_go_no_go_checklist:
(Check each before moving traffic gate)
- [ ] p95 within target for 48h in current gate window
- [ ] 5xx < threshold for 72h
- [ ] Observability spike dashboards green (no missing traces)
- [ ] Crashloop/backoff incidents none in past 24h
- [ ] GUI smoke tests pass (end-to-end sample flows)
- [ ] Key customer beta cohort acceptance recorded

Notes-to-self / open questions:
- Who will approve emergency GPU swap if Dedicated pool exhausted? (TBD: infra director)
- Verify billing alert thresholds with finance (ask: billing-alerts@redwood.ai)
- SLO for embedding tail latency (p99) needs clearer doc; proposal: p99 <= 1.2s for beta

Next immediate steps (owner -> due):
- Marco: lock initial commit for Dedicated pool + autoscale policy (due: 2025-01-20)
- Sana: add canary trace retention rule and confirm dashboard links (due: 2025-01-18)
- Priya: coordinate cross-functional dry-run w/ CS + Sales (dry-run date: 2025-01-28)

Historical decisions (short log):
- 2024-12-12: Decided to support model-v1-lite as fallback to guarantee p95 under surge. (RFC-201)
formatting_guidance: This is a live operational sheet; when updating metrics use the inline colored cells: green (on-target), amber (~10% drift), red (>10% drift). Annotate the cell with a short note and owner initials for any amber/red entries. Use linked_artifacts to tie back to tickets. Delete obsolete rows only after consensus in the #launch-runway Slack channel.
final_thoughts:
Keep this file terse; the canonical narrative lives on Confluence (linked above). The sheet is the action-focused ledger for the 8-week ramp — prefer checkboxes and single-line notes over long paragraphs.

-- Priya
